sources: https://parsonsadvocate.com/?p=73488 (secondary: April 2026 report of the concession award)

values.note: recreation.gov rate table: Peak Season (May 1 or May 18 - Oct 15) single site $20, single electric $30, double electric $50; the spring and fall first-come seasons ('No Water price') $16 single, $20 electric, $40 double electric. The Forest Service page lists only $16 / $20 / $40.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232008/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-18..10-15 and 2027-05-01..10-15: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 20, STANDARD ELECTRIC 30, STANDARD ELECTRIC-DOUBLE 50; First-come, First-served Seasons 2026-10-16..11-15, 2027-03-15..04-30: No Water price SNE 16, SE 20, DE 40) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/blue-bend-recreation-area-and-campground ('Single Site: $16 per night / Single Site with electric hook-up: $20 per night / Double Site with electric hook-up: $40 per night'), read 2026-10-21

hookups.source: RIDB catalog for facility 232008 (site 013 'RV ELECTRIC', reservable, Electricity Hookup 50, Water No, Sewer No; site 015 STANDARD ELECTRIC 30 A) + rec.gov rate table ('Campsite 13 Double Electric'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: 21 single-family sites along Anthony Creek, three with electric (13 and 15 bookable, 2 first-come); all back-in, catalog lengths 30-60 ft. Two group picnic shelters besides.

sites.source: RIDB catalog for facility 232008 (21 STANDARD/RV sites, every one Driveway Entry Back-In, Max Vehicle Length 30-60; 2 GROUP SHELTER) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232008 ('a selection of single family campsites and 2 picnic shelters'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Flush toilets and showers in summer only, vault toilets in spring and fall. Drinking water: recreation.gov says running water is seasonal with a hand pump in spring and fall, while the Forest Service page says 'Potable water is not available at this site'.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232008 ('Flush toilets and showers are available in summer, and vault toilets can be used through the spring and fall seasons. Running water is also seasonal, but a hand pump is available through spring and fall.') + Forest Service page (Restrooms 'Flush and Vault Toilets'; Water 'Potable water is not available at this site'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Forest Service: 'Late March - November/Possibly September'. recreation.gov takes reservations in the peak season (May - Oct 15) and lists first-come seasons from mid-March (2027) and to mid- or late November either side of it.

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/monongahela/recreation/blue-bend-recreation-area-and-campground (Seasons of Use 'Late March - November/Possibly September') + rec.gov rate seasons, read 2026-10-21. The derived 05-01/10-15 was the reservation calendar's edge, not the campground season.

values.note: Run by a concessioner since spring 2026: rec.gov's contact email is visit@svlandmgt.com, and the Parsons Advocate (April 2026) reports the Monongahela's permit for Lake Sherwood, Blue Bend and Pocahontas went to Sunshine Valley Land Management LLC. Only sites 13, 15, 19, 20 and 21 are reservable, in the peak season; the rest are first-come, and the spring and fall seasons are first-come only. Reservations close 4 days before arrival; one-night stays allowed; 14 days in any 30. Checkout 2 p.m. Access road can flood.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232008 (facility_email visit@svlandmgt.com; facility_rules minConsecutiveStay 1, reservationCutOff 4, maxStay 14 per rolling 30 days; notice 'Access Road Subject to FLOODING') + RIDB catalog (reservable flags) + rec.gov rate season names + Forest Service page ('Campground maximum length of stay is 14 days', 'Checkout time is 2:00 p.m.') + https://parsonsadvocate.com/?p=73488 (secondary, concession award), read 2026-10-21

summary: Hookups 50A confirmed manual (site 13); fees 16-40 -> 16-30 (single-site range; doubles $40-50 in the note); season derived 05-01/10-15 cleared for the Forest Service's 'Late March - November'; added sites (21, back-in, to 60 ft), facilities, booking (5 reservable sites, the rest FCFS, 14 max). Concessioner (Sunshine Valley Land Management) since 2026. AWH note left.
flags: Missing phone: recreation.gov gives '304-536-2144 for district office and 304-536-1440 for campground from May to August' and 'For facility specific information, please call (681) 368-0663'.

Operator: concession on federal land since spring 2026 (Sunshine Valley Land Management LLC, per rec.gov's svlandmgt.com contact email and a Parsons Advocate report); recreation.gov still marks it not commercially managed. Ownership federal is right; say concession-operated.
Official pages disagree on drinking water (rec.gov: seasonal running water + hand pump; Forest Service: 'Potable water is not available at this site'); potable_water left unset.
